attributes.name: Description
attributes.value: High-throughput gene expression profiling has become an important tool for investigating transcriptional activity in a variety of biological samples. To date, the vast majority of these experiments have focused on specific biological processes and perturbations. Here, we have generated and analyzed gene expression from a set of samples spanning a broad range of biological conditions. Specifically, we profiled gene expression from 91 human and mouse samples across a diverse array of tissues, organs, and cell lines. Because these samples predominantly come from the normal physiological state in the human and mouse, this dataset represents a preliminary, but substantial, description of the normal mammalian transcriptome. We have used this dataset to illustrate methods of mining these data, and to reveal insights into molecular and physiological gene function, mechanisms of transcriptional regulation, disease etiology, and comparative genomics. Finally, to allow the scientific community to use this resource, we have built a free and publicly accessible website (http://expression.gnf.org) that integrates data visualization and curation of current gene annotations. The terms of the Novartis data release policy prevent us from redistributing .cel files for this experiment, therefore there is no raw data, we hope to be able to release this in future.

attributes.value: RNA Modified Prep 1.Add 1 ml Trizol per 50 ?100mg of tissue or cells. 2.Add 20ul of 1ug/ul Glycogen  3.Homogenize  a.Hand held Polytron Homogenizer (for all tissues) for  1minute or b.20 gauge needle on a 5cc syringe (for cells only), pass  10 times or c.Qiagen homogenizer machine (for non-fibrous, and non-elastic tissues) 4.Incubate homogenized samples at room temperature for 5-10 minutes 5.Add 200ul of chloroform per 1 ml of Trizol used in step 1. 6.Vortex, incubate at room temp. for 3 minutes 7.Centrifuge at maximum speed, room temp, for 10 minutes 8.Isolate upper, aqueous phase and transfer to a new 1.5 ml tube 9.Add 500ul Isopropanol per 1 ml of Trizol used in step 1. 10.Vortex 11.Incubate at ?20C for 20 minutes 12.Centrifuge at maximum speed 4C for 20 minutes 13.Remove supernatant, keep pellet, don?t bother to dry  14.Resuspend  pellet in 100ul in RNAase free H20 15.Use Rneasy qiagen column to clean up total RNA. Elute total RNA off column with 25 ul  RNAase free H2O  twice for a total of 50ul.

Place QIAquick column in new collection tubes. Centrifuge column for an additional 1 min at maximum speed - Place QIAquick column in a clean 1.5-ml microfuge tube  - To elute DNA, add 30 ul Buffer EB (10 mM Tris-Cl, pH 8.5) to the center of the QIAquick column, let it sit for 1 min. then centrifuge for 1 min. Incubate 37°C for 4 -6 hours-gently mixing the reaction every 30 minutes - Clean up cRNA with QIAGEN RNeasy spin columns - Quantify the cRNA using Beckman DU640 Spectrophotometer  Fragmentation the cRNA for Target preparation - Remove 6x SSPE, then add 200 ul prewarmed buffer B and rotate the chip at 50C for 5 min - Remove buffer B and repeat above step and rotate for another 5 min at 50C - Cool chips with room temp buffer A -
